reason: The text describes the Egyptian Pharaoh complaining about the Hebrew/Israelite people to his own people (the Egyptians), not Hebrew leaders complaining about their people. The passage explicitly states 'the king' (הַמֶּלֶךְ, the Pharaoh) 'said to his people' (אֶל־עַמּוֹ) expressing concern that the Israelites are numerous and mighty. The complaint is Egyptian leadership expressing alarm about the Israelite population, not Hebrew leaders voicing grievances about their own people.
story: The Pharaoh turns on the Hebrews
